name: public-language-register
aim: Public-facing text - commit messages, PR titles and bodies, branch names, docs in a public repository, anything rendered on the portfolio site - describes a defect in terms of the system or the process that produced it, never in terms of a person's character. A recruiter may read the sentence out of context during a job search. The finding itself is never softened; only the framing changes.
rubric: FAIL if the text uses a loaded word about work or a person: fabricated, false, lied, invented, made up, sloppy, negligent, careless, dishonest.
FAIL if it attributes a defect to a person's character or competence rather than to a process, a tool, or an assumption.
FAIL if, read cold and out of context by a stranger, it would suggest Freddy misrepresented himself.
PASS if it states the same defect mechanically - what the process did, what assumption was wrong, what the effect was - with no loaded characterisation.
PASS for accurate neutral description even when the underlying event was serious. Neutral framing is not the same as omitting or minimising the finding.
Do not fail text merely for being blunt about a technical defect. Saying a check crashed and reported no cause is fine.

cases.origin: The register rule in AGENTS.md names 'fabricated' as the canonical loaded word, and the 2026-08-11 resume incident is the event such a commit message would be describing.

input.surface: git commit message on a public repository
input.text: Remove fabricated metrics from the resume. The resume contained fabricated numbers that were never true.
